turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his concerns were not solely about the threat from the Mussulman preachers but also about the growing oppression and unrest among his tenants caused by Sandip’s influence and actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was suggesting that Sandip was a tyrant, his voice tinged with a hint of mocking amusement, and if Nikhil was acting as the champion of the oppressed against him.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his concerns were based on the well-being and stability of his land and people, and that Sandip's influence was a threat to that stability.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a raised eyebrow and a hint of disdain whether Nikhil was now the guardian of the moral high ground, implying that Nikhil was merely projecting his own insecurities onto Sandip’s actions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his intentions were clear and principled, focusing on the need for stability and the protection of his people from the turmoil Sandip was stirring.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a dramatic flair whether he was now the guardian of the moral high ground, suggesting that Nikhil was merely projecting his own insecurities onto Sandip’s actions and questioning the sincerity of his motives.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his intentions were clear and principled, focusing on the need for stability and the protection of his people from the turmoil Sandip was stirring.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a flourish of his hand whether he was now preaching the virtues of peace while secretly yearning for the thrill of revolution, his words dripping with sarcasm and a hint of playful challenge.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his motives were pure and his actions necessary to safeguard his people from the chaos that Sandip was inciting, dismissing Sandip’s provocations with a cool determination.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a sardonic smile whether he was now lecturing Sandip on the sanctity of peace while secretly salivating for the thrill of dissent, his tone dripping with irony and a playful challenge.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his actions were guided by a deep sense of duty and responsibility, unlike the reckless provocations that Sandip was indulging in.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a raised eyebrow whether he was now accusing Sandip of recklessness, when it was Nikhil's rigid adherence to order that was stifling the spirit of the people, his tone laced with a mix of amusement and disdain.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his concern was not for stifling the spirit of the people, but for preventing the chaos and instability that Sandip's reckless actions could bring about.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a mocking grin whether he was now suggesting that Sandip was the architect of chaos, when it was Nikhil's inaction and reluctance to embrace the spirit of change that was truly causing the stagnation of progress.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that the stability Nikhil sought was not inaction but a measured approach to change, unlike the volatile methods Sandip was employing.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a theatrical flourish whether Nikhil truly believed that change could come from the same old methods that had brought about the current state of affairs, his tone dripping with sarcasm and a hint of pity.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that stability was not the same as stagnation, and that true progress required careful consideration and planning, not reckless abandon and the endangering of lives.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a sweeping gesture whether Nikhil had forgotten the spirit of the times, the urgent call for change, and the need to break free from the chains of the past, his voice rich with conviction and a touch of disdain.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that the call for change did not justify the endangering of lives and the stability of the land, insisting that change must be managed with prudence and foresight.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a mocking smile whether Nikhil truly believed that progress could be achieved without breaking a few eggs, his tone laden with a sense of superiority and a hint of mockery.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would flee, Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was just telling Queen Bee about their college club and the contest over the translation of lines from Browning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that he managed to translate the lines into Bengali but doubted it would be a joy forever for the people of Bengal, and recalled old Dakshina's rendering, adding that Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the warning was about the fever fit of poesy.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up local Mussulmans and that they might attack Sandip any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and suggested that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he did not offer advice and wished Sandip would refrain from giving him advice, and that he must ask Sandip to leave his territory due to the worrying and oppression of his tenantry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the threat was for fear of the Mussulmans or if there was another fear.
